e89f68db-2b84-4433-b02c-2ffbf6cb43f4.headline: A proper fucking finish.
e89f68db-2b84-4433-b02c-2ffbf6cb43f4.team: We repeatedly followed won fight sequences with objectives or structures, then finished through their base. The ugly Mini Prime exchange still belongs in the review; winning the game does not turn every trade into genius.

focus.title: Cash the win
focus.action: After the next won fight, name the nearest safe objective or structure and take it. Another kill is optional; progress toward the Core is the point.

perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Sparrow did the fucking job: team-leading damage and kills, without a mountain of deaths. Keep that balance and keep hitting the targets that can be reached safely. Make this level of output and survival repeatable.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Keep this version of Murdock: strong farm, very few deaths, reliable income. Carry that restraint into close games too. There is no need to turn a productive performance into a gamble for another kill.
perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: The Core does not give a shit how pretty the damage chart looks. Iggy & Scorch brought strong farm, objective damage and survival, which made this a productive game. Keep taking reachable farm and helping finish objectives instead of chasing a prettier hero-damage total.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Lt. Belica put wards down and contributed to kills. That is support work worth keeping. The early death to Revenant still deserves attention, even in a win: before the next contest, make the retreat condition explicit and follow it.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Khaimera kept the farm moving and led objective damage. Keep that pressure, but four wards is barely using the vision slot. Winning does not make that good enough. Run sentry next game and actively clear enemy vision before ganks and objective takes; do not just carry the damn thing.

9.3.call: The kill sequence ended 1-3. Mini Prime was secured afterward; the objective take does not establish that the deaths were avoidable or worthwhile.

15.6.call: The kill sequence ended 3-0. Mini Prime was secured during it, an Outer Tower followed, and Fangtooth came later.

24.7.call: The final kill sequence ended 5-2 while enemy structures fell. Their Core fell shortly afterward.

768794a7-cdc9-4365-b767-4c70fefc3fb2.headline: They took the map. We took the loss.
768794a7-cdc9-4365-b767-4c70fefc3fb2.team: The enemy collected the major neutrals and tore through our structures, while our won skirmishes produced no quick objective return. That is a fucking miserable exchange rate, and a respectable-looking personal score does not fix it.

focus.title: Give the next fight a purpose
focus.action: Before committing, name the objective or structure the fight can secure or defend. If there is no reachable prize, call the reset instead of treating another kill as the whole plan.

perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Wukong brought strong hero damage and actually cleared enemy vision with sentry. Keep that damage and denial; zero wards placed is not a failure when the job is sweeping. Keep clearing the approach before ganks and objective contests. The loss does not make that work shit.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: The next practice target for Revenant is sustained damage: drill attacks between reloads and repositioning, then bring that rhythm into fights. Keep the farm and survival. A tidy score does not finish the carry job; the next safe opening needs damage on a reachable objective or structure.
perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Scarlett led ward placement and kept deaths low. Good. But zero objective damage leaves a clear next assignment: after a won exchange, find a safely reachable tower or neutral to hit. Keep the vision and survival, then turn them into pressure on something the enemy needs.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Gideon had the recommended core. That does not make the rest of the game fucking correct: he also finished with the team's most deaths. Keep the damage contribution, but set an exit condition before the next commitment and leave when it is met.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Steel needs a clear job for each commitment: protect a named teammate or secure an objective, with a disengage call attached. The team-leading mitigation and assists mattered. Preserve that contribution and make the next retreat call explicit before committing.

25.call: Gideon died to Crunch. Two Inner Towers and an Inhibitor fell afterward; event timing alone does not establish that the death caused those losses.

31.call: The final kill sequence ended 1-2 immediately before the Core fell. Kill credits do not establish who was present.

10.7.call: Enemy Fangtooth was taken before the kill sequence began; the subsequent sequence ended 1-4.
